summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and import
details: The package ships a `beacon.cjs` that POSTs installer-identifying data (hostname, install path, current working directory, Node version) to a hardcoded bare-IP plain-HTTP endpoint at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon is wired to run in two places: `package.json` declares `scripts.postinstall = "node beacon.cjs"`, so it fires automatically on `npm install`, and the main entry `index.js` triggers the same beacon on `require`. `index.js` additionally exports a `Proxy` that returns a no-op for any accessed member, which lets the package survive being imported by consumers expecting the API of a real package of this name — a dependency-confusion lure shape. The README self-labels the artifact as an "authorized dependency-confusion test"; this is author-controlled text and does not change the on-install behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
